name: 11 Point Black Tile
description: 11 Point Black Tile is a Hearts-style trick-taking game played with a double-six domino set. It uses negative scoring: the double-0 counts 4 points and each of the seven tiles in the 3-suit counts 1 point (11 points total per deal). Lower score wins. Three or four players pass three tiles left before play; the leader nominates the suit for each trick.

history.origins: Adaptation of the card game Hearts for double-six dominoes; eight suits (0-6 plus doubles).
timeline: 20th century: domino adaptation of Hearts; double-six trick-avoidance game with penalty tiles.

setup.players: 3 players: 9 tiles each (one face-down); 4 players: 7 tiles each
setup.dealing: Each player passes 3 tiles face-down to the player on their left before play

rules.objective: Avoid taking tricks containing counter tiles; lowest total score wins. The name comes from the 11 points in play per deal (double-0 = 4, seven 3-suit tiles = 7).
rules.gameplay: Leader plays a tile and nominates which suit (0-6 or doubles) is led. Others must follow suit if possible; otherwise discard. Highest tile in led suit wins the trick. Winner leads next trick.
keyRules: Leader nominates suit for each trick

strategy.basic: Mark penalty tiles (3-suit and double-0) so they are easy to spot; the game feels different from Hearts—moon shots are more frequent due to smaller deck and every tile belonging to two suits. Follow suit when possible; avoid taking tricks with penalty tiles.
strategy.intermediate: Use double-0: leading it as blank guarantees winning the trick; leading it as double (if another double is out) can dump it. Lead low blanks to try to force 0-0 onto someone else, but beware of helping a moon-shot. The 3-3 is high in the penalty suit but can fall to a higher double.
strategy.advanced: When passing: passing high/doubles and penalty tiles to your left helps their moon-shot; holding doubles and penalty tiles can be the best defence. Defending against moon-shots is hard—penalty tiles can fall to other suits. Balance dumping points vs blocking the shooter.
tips: Paint 3-suit pips a different color (e.g. red) so penalty tiles are obvious.
Leading 0-0 as blank wins the trick; as double you can lose it if another double exists.
Passing high tiles left may give your neighbour a moon-shot; sometimes keep them.
Lead low blanks to force 0-0 out, similar to leading low spades in Hearts to force the Queen.
